candidates.title: Hybrid Compression of Large Language Models using Structured Pruning and Quantization
candidates.venue: International Conference Intelligent Data Communication Technologies and Internet Things
candidates.abstract: The evolution of Large Language Models (LLMs) such as GPT has been incredible, and natural language generation is the area that these models have almost entirely taken over. Their huge size and number of parameters—over a billion—still create problems related to storage, memory, and computation, especially when it comes to deploying at the edge. Compression techniques such as pruning and quantization greatly help with these issues, but picking one often implies giving up some accuracy, efficiency, and the ability to generalize. A new hybrid compression technique is proposed in this study, which combines the two: structured pruning and quantization. The structure is first pruned by getting rid of the whole low-importance attention heads and neurons, among which the biggest part of the computational cost is. After the pruning, quantization is applied to weights and activations to convert them into low-bit representation. This representation greatly increases memory saving and speeds up the process. Quantization of this type secures that it will only take place on the most vital parts, thus, the least accuracy will be lost and, in the opposite, the size of the compression will be the most. The experimental results on the GPT-2 model confirm our method leads to a remarkable reduction in the number of parameters, and inference times along with a slight drop in performance, thus enabling the application of large models on resource-limited platforms.
candidates.reason: 構造化プルーニングで低重要度の注意ヘッドとニューロンを除去した後に重み・活性化を低ビット量子化するハイブリッド圧縮を提案し、エッジ配備でのメモリ削減と高速化を狙うLLM推論向け圧縮の直接的貢献が要旨で確認できる。

candidates.title: Layer-Wise Weight Sharing for Efficient Transformer on SoCs
candidates.venue: International Conference on Fog and Edge Computing
candidates.abstract: Transformer-based models such as BERT have achieved remarkable success across a wide range of natural language processing tasks. However, deploying them on resource-constrained devices, including System-on-Chips (SoCs), remains challenging due to limited memory and computational capacity of these devices. Weight sharing has proved to be an effective approach for significantly reducing model size, yet designing an efficient layer-wise weight sharing framework that achieves high compression while maintaining model performance and low latency is not a trivial task. In this paper, we systematically analyze the impact of key weight sharing hyperparameters on model performance, model size, and latency, and propose a Genetic Algorithm-based optimization framework to automatically identify the optimal configuration for each layer—balancing performance, compression ratio, and inference speed. Additionally, through targeted modifications and efficient on-the-fly decompression, we demonstrate that the proposed weight sharing framework introduces no additional latency overhead and can even reduce inference time. Compared to uniform compression, our approach makes transformer blocks with substantially lower memory requirements and reduced latency while maintaining competitive performance across evaluation metrics.
candidates.reason: BERT等のTransformerをSoCへ載せるため層ごとの重み共有ハイパーパラメータを遺伝的アルゴリズムで最適化し、オンザフライ展開で追加レイテンシなくモデルサイズ削減と推論時間短縮を両立させる手法であり、オンデバイス推論圧縮の直接的貢献が確認できる。

candidates.title: Fewer Bits, More Tries: Recovering Capability Under Memory Constraints
candidates.abstract: Large language models are generally more capable than smaller ones, but their memory requirements can make local deployment difficult. We ask whether part of this capability gap can instead be recovered by running a smaller or more compressed model multiple times and selecting among its outputs using public or model-generated tests. Single-user local inference can leave hardware underutilized, allowing parallel candidate generation to trade additional test-time computation for accuracy at modest latency cost. Across four code-generation benchmarks, verified retry recovers substantial accuracy lost to model size or compression. A 7B Qwen model with eight parallel attempts essentially matches a 32B model on MBPP+ and exceeds it on the other three benchmarks, while using about $4\times$ less model memory, running up to $6\times$ faster, and using less energy, as measured on Nvidia GPU. We observe similar tradeoff across model sizes, compression levels and hardware choices, although exact benefit depends on the hardware profile and problem setting. These results show that model capacity can be traded for verified test-time computation when correct solutions remain reachable within a modest retry budget.
candidates.reason: メモリ制約下のローカル推論で小さい・圧縮されたモデルを複数回並列に試行しテストで検証して選択することで、7Bモデル8回試行が32Bに匹敵しつつメモリ約4分の1で済むことを示す、圧縮と並列候補生成を組み合わせた推論戦略の直接的貢献が確認できる。

candidates.title: Analog-AI Hardware Accelerators for Low-Latency Transformer-Based Language Models (Invited)
candidates.abstract: Analog Non-Volatile Memory-based accelerators offer highthroughput and energy-efficient Multiply-Accumulate operations for the large Fully-Connected layers that dominate Transformer-based Large Language Models (LLMs). We describe recent chip-demo and architectural efforts, quantify the unique benefits of Fully- (rather than Partially-) Weight-Stationary systems, and discuss factors affecting latency of token-processing and generation.
candidates.reason: アナログ不揮発メモリによるMACアクセラレータでTransformer系LLMの全結合層を処理し、完全重み定常方式の利点やトークン処理・生成のレイテンシ要因を論じる低レイテンシ推論向けハードウェアの直接的貢献が要旨で確認できる。

candidates.title: MC-MLA: Accelerating Multi-Head Latent Attention on RISC-V Many-Core Chips
candidates.venue: International Symposium on Computer Science and Intelligent Control
candidates.abstract: As the core mechanism of the DeepSeek-V3 model, Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA) significantly reduces the computational complexity by low-rank matrix factorization. However, the memory access overhead and computing bottlenecks are becoming increasingly prominent as the sequence length continues to grow. The performance of this mechanism is severely limited by the efficiency of memory access. Meanwhile, existing research on MLA acceleration mostly relies on NVIDIA GPUs and the CUDA ecosystem, which significantly constrains the expansion of its application scenario. Given this, this paper proposes Many-Core Optimized Multi-Head Latent Attention (MC-MLA), which is committed to achieving efficient parallel acceleration of MLA on a many-core RISC-V architecture. The scheme includes two core optimizations: (1) KV Reuse-Oriented Parallel Dataflow Optimization: For the matrix absorption characteristics in MLA, we design an online transposition dataflow that absorbs value matrices into key matrices. This approach ensures efficient reuse of KV-Cache while achieving pipeline overlap between data movement and computation, thereby reducing memory access pressure and hiding latency for KV-Cache load operations. (2) Balanced Tree-like Inter-Core Reduction Algorithm based on Semaphore: This algorithm resolves workload imbalance in high-parallel scenarios, significantly promoting many-core collaboration efficiency. The experimental results demonstrate that MC-MLA can enhance the computational efficiency of MLA under various configurations of batch size, number of heads, and sequence length. Final comparison results reveal that MC-MLA effectively alleviates key bottlenecks: load imbalance in reduction operations and NoC congestion in memory accesses, achieving up to $1.69 \times$ performance improvement and 76 % of bandwidth utilization. This competitive implementation provides a reference for MLA adaptation and performance optimization on similar many-core architectures.
candidates.reason: DeepSeek-V3のMulti-Head Latent AttentionをRISC-Vメニーコアで高速化するMC-MLAで、KV再利用向け並列データフローと行列吸収によるオンライン転置によりKVキャッシュのメモリアクセス圧力を下げレイテンシを隠蔽する、注意機構・KVキャッシュ最適化の直接的貢献が確認できる。
